source.title: With Greater Distance Comes Worse Performance: On the Perspective of Layer Utilization and Model Generalization

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper sweeps fully connected network width and label noise, then measures generalization and layer utilization. Its distance-from-initialization measure is related to, but different from, V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for network size, label noise, utilization, generalization, and layer contribution. Figure-only values are not recoverable from the supplied text. Reinitialization is discussed as a regularizer, but no separate quantitative post-reinitialization outcome is stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study varies network width and label noise and reports model-wise double descent in its own experiments. Appendix A.2 explicitly identifies a second descent in generalization, bearing on V2, although the measured outcome is a training–test loss gap rather than classification test error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that deeper-layer distance from initialization estimates effective model complexity and predicts generalization error, that deeper layers tend to capture training noise, and that rolling final layers back to initialization can reduce overfitting. These conclusions concern fully connected networks.
record.recipe_differences: Fully connected ReLU networks trained with SGD on MNIST and CIFAR10; the study varies label noise and hidden-layer size and measures distance from initialization and layer contribution. It does not reproduce the original claim's experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported patterns vary with hidden-layer size, label-noise ratio, dataset, and layer depth. The paper states that CIFAR10 places more models in the under-parameterized regime under the selected sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Deeper-layer distance from initialization correlates positively with training–test loss gaps and recovered-label loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater deeper-layer movement from initialization predicts worse generalization and recovered-label performance in these width and noise sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: Reinitializing deeper layers generally lowers test and recovered-label losses, whereas reinitializing earlier layers generally raises them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early layers tend to learn transferable features, while deeper layers can contribute harmful memorization that layer reinitialization partly removes.

record.problems: The experiments use only fully connected networks and two datasets. Testing-loss convergence is acknowledged as uncertain. The main results are displayed in figures without numeric values in the supplied text, and each experiment uses three MNIST runs and six CIFAR10 runs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Reinitialization is described as a proposed post-training regularizer, but the supplied text does not state a separate quantitative before/after outcome to record as an intervention result.

untested.parts: No reported comparison establishes nearly perfect fitting of fully random labels, chance held-out accuracy for those labels, and strong natural-label held-out accuracy using the same recipe.

Classification test-error values, improvement at each successive post-interpolation width, and the original one-hidden-layer recipe are not established. Testing-loss convergence is explicitly uncertain.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Extend R1–R2 beyond the interpolation peak to include the explicitly reported second descent in generalization and the qualitative near-perfect training fits in the over-parameterized regime. Numeric values and dataset-specific descent magnitudes cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: The introduction's description of steadily improving post-interpolation test risk is attributed to prior work; the verdict instead relies on this study's Figure 3 discussion and Appendix A.2. A smaller loss gap alone need not imply lower test loss, so the V2 support remains qualitative.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization; the paper varies a fraction of shuffled labels but does not report the V1 comparison.
The width and data-complexity sweep examines generalization around an interpolation threshold, but the text does not state the post-threshold test-error trend required by V2.
The experiments use fully connected networks and do not compare them with convolutional networks.
Only SGD is reported; adaptive optimizers are not compared.
Batch size and fixed-epoch batch comparisons are not reported.
The study measures distance from initialization, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, and does not compare that measure against norm- or margin-based measures.
The study does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: 5 fully connected layers with ReLU
rows.size_stated: Hidden layer sizes varied; exact sizes not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Compared final-layer utilization with generalization and resilience across models
rows.measure: Association between layer utilization and generalization/resilience
rows.value: The merged curves for deeper layers are positively correlated with generalization and resilience; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: Utilization is defined as distance between trained weights and initial weights. This differs from V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
rows.check: Distance from initialization is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness. Positive correlation is with the loss gap and recovered-label loss: larger values indicate worse outcomes, rather than better generalization or resilience.

rows.operation_detail: Reinitialized individual layer weights to initial values and measured contribution to testing loss
rows.measure: Layer contribution to testing loss, defined as loss after reinitialization minus loss before reinitialization
rows.value: Early layers generally contribute positively; deeper layers generally have negative contribution to testing loss; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The supplied text describes the contribution pattern but does not provide the underlying values.
rows.check: Layer reinitialization does not test any listed version. The baseline is the same trained model before reinitialization. Positive contribution means reinitialization raises test loss; negative contribution means it lowers test loss.

relationships.condition: Five-layer fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10, across width and label-noise sweeps, trained with SGD for 10,000 epochs.
relationships.reason: R1–R2 capture the interpolation peak; the supporting post-threshold result comes from Appendix A.2, which explicitly reports a second descent in generalization and describes near-perfect training fits in the over-parameterized regime. Evidence is qualitative and based on loss gaps.
relationships.display_finding: The absolute difference between training and test loss showed a second descent. The study did not establish decreasing classification error after zero training error or convergence of test loss.
